en_note: Manually curated for a Quranic root occurring exactly twice.
meaning: The root بَسَرَ (basara) has two cores per Ibn Fāris: unripeness — a thing taken before its time, whence بُسْر, unripe dates — and a face's stopping or setting hard, whence بَاسِر, a scowling countenance.
meaning_source: Derived from the classical dictionaries (chiefly Maqayis al-Lugha, Ibn Faris d.1004) held in lexicon_full/
